Read this first

The honest summary

These strategies survived the rules. They did not make money.

Every account stayed inside the 5% daily and 10% static loss limits for the whole eight months — no breaches, no blown accounts. But the funded stages landed in April–August 2026, and in that stretch nothing worked.

The strategies were built and tuned only on 2025 data, then run once through the test window. That separation is the reason these numbers are worth anything, and it is also why they are disappointing: gold in 2026 did not behave like gold in 2025.

The single most useful finding here is not a strategy. It is that during April–August 2026 every concept tested was unprofitable — trend following and mean reversion alike. That is a property of the market in those months, not a failure to find the right indicator, and no amount of further searching would have fixed it without simply fitting to that chop.

Diagnosis

Why the edge disappeared

Gold's daily ATR roughly doubled between the two periods, from 1.44% to 2.38% of price, while monthly moves flipped from a steady climb to violent two-way swings: +12.6%, +11.3%, −12.8%, −10.7%, +10.7%. All four at once

Running four accounts only helps if they can fail independently. These cannot. Average pairwise correlation of daily P&L is 0.39, and the two that got funded — A3 and A4 — are the most correlated pair of the lot, because every surviving strategy is a trend-continuation strategy on the same instrument. Four accounts here is closer to one position at four times the size than to a diversified book.

The four

What each strategy actually does

A1 Donchian H1 Breakout

Buys a break of the highest high of the last 45 hourly bars and sells the mirror image, whenever ADX confirms the market is actually moving. The channel defines its own trend, so no separate trend filter is applied.

Signal
45-bar H1 Donchian break
Stop
2.5 x H1 ATR
Target
5R, trailing from 2R
Filter
ADX(14) > 18
Risk
1.00% per trade
Cap
2 trades / 2 losses per day

A2 H1 Trend Pullback

Waits for an established H1 and H4 uptrend, lets price pull back into the H1 20-EMA, then enters when an hourly bar reasserts the trend. The stop sits behind structure rather than at an arbitrary distance.

A3 Donchian H4 Swing

The channel idea on a four-hour clock: a break of the 20-bar H4 extreme with a stop of one H4 ATR. Fewer, longer trades that hold through noise the hourly version gets shaken out by.

The search

Everything that was tried and thrown away

15 concepts were tested on 2025 data and 10 were discarded outright; one more was losing until a wider stop rescued it. Every counter-trend idea lost money at every parameter setting tried, which is why all four survivors are trend strategies — not because the set was chosen that way.

Method

How this was tested

  1. Real bid and ask. Dukascopy M1 candles for both sides of the book, Jan 2025 – Aug 2026. Longs fill at the ask and exit at the bid, shorts the reverse, so the spread is measured from the feed rather than assumed. Median spread was $0.62.
  2. Dead minutes removed. 21% of the raw feed is zero-volume padding for hours when gold is shut. Left in, it decays a weekend ATR toward zero and every ATR-scaled stop comes out far too tight.
  3. Costs charged. $7 per lot round-turn commission, $0.05 slippage on entries, $0.15 against every stop-out. A bar that covers both the stop and the target is scored as a stop.
  4. No lookahead. Signals computed on bar t execute at bar t+1's open.
  5. Rules enforced on equity, not balance. The 5% daily and 10% static limits are checked against intrabar equity including open P&L, which is how accounts actually die.
  6. Built on 2025, tested once on the rest. Parameters were chosen by sweeping 2025 data and picking the middle of broad plateaus, never single best cells.

Caveats

What would make me distrust this

One market, one period

Eight months of one instrument is a handful of independent trends, not a statistical sample. The development window was a single strong uptrend, which is the easiest possible regime for the strategies that won.

The test window was consulted

The strategies were fixed before the test ran, but after seeing the result I went back and changed two things in the engine: how a position is sized when the minimum lot is too large, and the order of the stop and breach checks within a bar. Both are corrections rather than tuning, and both were re-checked on 2025 data — but the final numbers are no longer purely out of sample.

A $6,000 account is small for gold

At $4,000–5,000 an ounce with 2–3% daily ranges, a sensible ATR-based stop is $30–75 wide. The 0.01 lot minimum then risks $30–75, which is 0.5–1.25% of the account, so position sizing has almost no resolution and some valid setups cannot be taken at all.

Simulated fills are optimistic by nature

Real slippage clusters exactly where these strategies trade — breakouts and news. The modelled $0.15 against stops is a reasonable average, not a bad day.

If you actually do this

What I would tell you

  • Do not run four correlated accounts. At 0.39 average correlation you are paying four fees for close to one bet. Either trade one account, or find edges that fail at different times — which, on gold alone, this search could not do.
  • A3 and A4 are the two worth keeping. They held most of their edge into the test window (+0.267 and +0.322 R per trade) and were the only two to get funded, while A1 and A2 collapsed to near zero (+0.014 and +0.082).
  • Expect the challenge to be the easy part. Three of the four passed Phase 1 and two got funded in under four months. Staying profitable afterwards is where this fell apart, and that is where the money actually is.
  • Watch the daily limit, not just the total. A3's worst day in the funded stage was −4.51% against a 5% hard stop. One more losing trade that day and the account was gone.
  • The reset option is the real cost driver. At $59.99 a reset, a strategy that gets funded slowly and dies quickly is worse than one that never passes.

Backtest on Dukascopy XAUUSD M1 bid/ask data, 1 Jan 2025 – 19 Aug 2026. Simulated results from historical data; they are not a prediction and not investment advice.
